chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us in Nahawand in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the month of Ramadan in the year 229 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated to us from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said:
Allah does not consent save to reverse the timing of the diviners.

key_terms.الْمَوْقِتِينَ: Diviners or those who calculate and predict specific times for events, especially the reappearance of the Imam.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the timing of the Mahdi's appearance and those who predict it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as), the phrase 'Allah wills to reverse the timing of the timers' highlights the divine prerogative to alter the calculated dates of the occultation and reappearance, thereby invalidating specific predictions made by astrologers and scholars. This serves as a critical theological principle in Shia eschatology, emphasizing that while the general timeframe is known, the exact moment remains hidden to test the faith of the believers. It underscores the concept of 'Ghaybah' (occultation) not as a delay, but as a divinely managed period where human calculations are subject to God's will.
